title: Body Systems of Plants and Animals
seo_title: Primary 3 Basic Science: Body Systems of Plants and Animals Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 3 Basic Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Plants have parts (roots, stems, leaves, flowers) that work together to take in water and make food. Animals, including humans, have body systems, such as the digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems, whose organs work together. (summary of the Basic Science curriculum, Primary 3, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 Basic Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): parts of a plant, how water moves in plants, the digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Body parts work together in systems.
key_sub: Roots take in water; leaves make food.
body_html:
How to think about it

In plants, the roots take in water and minerals, the stem carries water up and holds the plant, and the leaves make food using sunlight. Flowers make seeds.

In animals, organs work together in systems. The digestive system breaks down food; the respiratory system takes in oxygen through the lungs; the circulatory system (heart and blood vessels) carries food and oxygen around the body.

Example

Which organ pumps blood?

In your chest

Answer: the heart

Example

Which plant part takes in water?

Under the ground

Answer: the roots

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get food from the soil.
  • Mixing up the lungs and the stomach.
  • Thinking the heart is in the stomach.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the air or the roots?
c: They happen at the same time.
Water does not pass through either.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Tobi stood a stick of celery in a jar of water with red food colouring. Where will the red colour appear after a day?

items.e: The coloured water travels up the stem to the top of the plant.

items.q: Nonso stood a white rose in a jar of water with green food colouring. Why does the colour spread up the plant?

items.q: Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?

items.e: Plants need light to make food.

items.q: Why does a plant droop (wilt) when it does not get enough water?

items.q: Which organ system holds the body up and protects organs?

items.q: What is the job of the alveoli?

A sheet of muscle under the lungs that contracts and flattens when we breathe in.

items.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
